verdicts.quote: a building or part of a building where a particular kind of animal is kept or a particular activity happens, with the purpose named before the word
verdicts.reason: This definition does not fit tree house or guest house, which are listed as examples and collocations, and it wrongly implies that the first element always names a purpose.

verdicts.reason: The example uses an unapproved personal reference; only the specified list of personal names may be used.

verdicts.quote: one of the groups of elected people who make the laws of a country, or the building where they meet
verdicts.reason: The building meaning is not part of the usual political sense of house; house means a chamber or branch of a legislature, not normally its meeting building.

verdicts.quote: a restaurant, bar, hotel, or similar business, seen as the one that provides what its customers get
verdicts.reason: This is overbroad and conflates several construction-specific uses, including house wine and house rules; house rules are not necessarily rules of a restaurant, bar, or hotel.

verdicts.quote: "countability": "singular only"
verdicts.reason: House in this institutional-provider sense is countable: different houses may have different house rules or house styles.

verdicts.quote: In a card game at a casino, the house keeps a small share of every bet.
verdicts.reason: A casino is not a restaurant, bar, hotel, or similar business under the definition, so the example demonstrates an uncovered meaning.

verdicts.quote: "house rules"
verdicts.reason: House rules commonly means rules set by any organization, game, or household, not specifically by the customer-provider sense defined here.

verdicts.quote: an old and important family, especially one of kings or queens, over many generations
verdicts.reason: A house can be a noble, royal, or ruling family and need not be old; "old" is an unnecessary restriction.
